review_candidates.title: National Reporting, Monitoring and Evaluation Officer
review_candidates.description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates as well as external women candidates are considered as first-tier candidates. Organizational Context and Scope Within the IOM OPT Mission, the Programme Support Unit (PSU) is a cross-sectoral unit working closely with all thematic units to support the development, implementation, monitoring and reporting of projects and other initiatives. The unit coordinates closely with HQ and regional colleagues, as well as external counterparts and donors to support quality and well-coordinated programming and oversight. This includes supporting the implementation and monitoring of the mission-wide IOM OPT strategy. Under the overall supervision of the Head of Programmes and direct supervision of the Programme Support Officer, the National Reporting, Monitoring and Evaluation Officer will support the implementation of projects/programmes/strategy Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) activities for the mission, as well as contribute to report drafting and review, in line with internal and donor requirements. Responsibilities M&E Framework Support the development and updating of the overall framework for IOM OPT, including indicators, tools and methodologies for ad hoc, monthly, quarterly and annual monitoring processes, remote and third-party monitoring, ensuring alignment with donor agreements and RBM guidance. Ensure effective financial planning and oversight of M&E activities, including appropriate budgeting and regular expenditure monitoring, tracking of commitments and burn rates, identification of variances, and timely follow-up on required budget adjustments, in coordination with the Programme Support Unit and relevant Resource Management colleagues. Support the development, testing and updating of standardized M&E tools and assist in promoting their consistent use through training and follow-up with programme focal points and implementing partners. Support integration of protection, gender and inclusion considerations into monitoring frameworks and tools in coordination with the Protection focal point. Support the maintenance and application of remote monitoring and emergency-adapted tools for access-constrained environments and rapid onset situations. Evaluation and Learning Support the planning and coordination of internal and external evaluations, including drafting of Terms of Reference, facilitating evaluation missions, coordinating with evaluators, and tracking of recommendations. Third Party Monitoring Support the implementation and coordination of third-party monitoring arrangements including preparation of TPM scopes of work, tools, and deliverables. Review TPM reports, validate findings and support integration of results into programme follow-up and learning processes. Monitoring, Data Quality and Reporting Support regular progress tracking against indicators and contribute to quarterly updates to the mission, in coordination with programme focal points. Support data verification and validation through data quality checks, consistency checks, field spot checks (when feasible) and review of implementing partner submissions. Ensure adherence to IOM’s data protection principles and proper handling of sensitive data. Coordinate with the Programme Support Officer to support timely preparation of donor reports reflecting results against agreed indicators log frames, and stakeholder information needs, providing analytical inputs to results sections and ensuring coherence between narrative and quantitative data. Review IM and monitoring reports, identify bottlenecks and propose necessary corrective actions. Support development of dashboards and visual analytical products. Support tracking risks and assumptions across projects and coordinate with programme teams to update mitigation measures and adjust monitoring plans accordingly. Management Contribute to capacity-building activities for staff and implementing partners on M&E, RBM, data collection, accountability and reporting. Keep abreast of developments in IOM’s Evaluation and Monitoring and Results-Based Management (RBM) functions to support compliance with IOM monitoring and reporting requirements, including for the Strategic Results Framework (SRF), the Institutional Questionnaire (IQ), Project Information and Management Application ( PRIMA), and other regional M&E planning tools. Perform other duties as may be assigned. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education Master’s degree in international relations, Political or Social Sciences, Business or Public Administration, Law or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or Bachelor’s degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience Other relevant training related to the field of monitoring and evaluation are added advantage. Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience Demonstrated technical knowledge in project development, quantitative and qualitative M&E methods and data collection and analysis, and reporting, with understanding of contemporary trends and innovations in the field of monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL). Experience in RBM, logical frameworks and other strategic planning approaches; implementation of M&E systems and plans; training in M&E development and implementation; information analysis and report writing. Proven experience in data management, analysis and reporting in a humanitarian context. Skills Strong analytical skills and organization skills. Good knowledge of research methodologies and quantitative and qualitative techniques. Strong writing, presentation, and facilitation. Advanced knowledge of MS office and working knowledge of databases and statistical tools. Ability to meet deadlines and produce clearly and accurate written reports. Languages All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish). For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written). Fluency in Arabic is an added advantage. Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments. Required Competencies IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link . Competencies will be assessed during the selection process. Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values: Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion. Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct. Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges. Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance. Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated. Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2 Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results. Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes. Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate. Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work. Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way. Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2, if with direct reports Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential. Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential. Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty. Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction. Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings. Notes Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category. Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months. Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances. IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities. IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts. IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here ). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application. No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

review_candidates.title: Humanitarian Access and Safety (HAS) officer Niger Maradi
review_candidates.description: Job Description Tous les employés du NRC doivent travailler conformément aux valeurs de l'organisation. Être dévoué , innovant , inclusif et responsable sont des attitudes et des convictions qui doivent guider nos actions et nos relations. NRC s'engage en faveur de la sécurité et du bien-être et, ensemble, nous construisons une culture de travail positive pour se sentir valorisé, responsabilisé, soutenu, en sécurité et avoir un sentiment d'appartenance. Le NRC ne tolère pas que des employés exploitent ou abusent des gens et a une tolérance zéro face à l'inaction. L'objectif de la fonction Accès et Sécurité Humanitaires (HAS) du NRC est de permettre une réponse humanitaire basée sur des principes et sûre, pour les communautés et les partenaires avec lesquels nous travaillons ainsi que pour notre personnel. Malgré le succès du NRC à fournir une assistance aux personnes dans le besoin, les contraintes de sécurité et d'accès restent des défis importants. Des obstacles tels que les conflits et la violence, les défis environnementaux et physiques, les obstacles bureaucratiques et l'ingérence dans les opérations humanitaires entravent la fourniture de services et de protection aux personnes déplacées. Responsibilities Rôle et responsabilités L'agent technique Accès et sécurité humanitaires (HAS) fournit une gamme de soutien en matière d'accès humanitaire, de sûreté et de sécurité dans la zone. Sous la supervision directe du responsable de secteur et avec le soutien technique et la supervision du responsable HAS, l'agent technique HAS soutient la mise en œuvre et le suivi de la politique, des plans, des procédures, des trackers et des processus HAS du NRC dans le bureau de zone et les bureaux locaux connexes (le cas échéant ). Ce rôle nécessite une présence fréquente sur le terrain pour soutenir l'exécution sûre et fondée sur des principes des programmes et le devoir de diligence du personnel du NRC. Responsabilités génériques (max 10) Soutenir la mise en œuvre du système de gestion mondial des HAS de NRC au niveau de la zone, préparer les rapports nécessaires et exécuter les éléments du plan opérationnel de la HAS axés sur la zone. Contribuer à une culture permettant une réponse humanitaire sûre et fondée sur des principes et soutenir la mise en œuvre de normes minimales de programmation sûre et inclusive. Soutenir l'élaboration de documents HAS au niveau de la zone, y compris les plans d'urgence, les stratégies d'accès et les procédures opérationnelles standard (PON), conformément aux normes organisationnelles. Maintenir une compréhension du contexte humanitaire de la zone et informer régulièrement la direction de la zone des principaux développements en matière de sécurité, de l'exposition du NRC, des problèmes d'accès et des menaces émergentes afin d'éclairer la prise de décision. Aider le gestionnaire/coordonnateur des HAS à évaluer les risques de sécurité et les évaluations des accès, y compris les évaluations rapides des risques pour les nouveaux sites opérationnels, en collaborant avec la direction pour identifier et mettre en œuvre des mesures d'atténuation pertinentes et soutenir la programmation sûre. Effectuer des exercices et former le personnel sur les sujets liés à l'accès, à la sûreté et à la sécurité et offrir des séances d'information régulières. En coordination avec le supérieur hiérarchique et le responsable HAS, assurer la liaison avec les agences des Nations Unies, les ONG, les autorités locales et d'autres acteurs externes afin de partager et d'obtenir des informations sur la sécurité afin d'éclairer les opérations et la gestion de la sécurité, ainsi que d'accroître l'accès humanitaire et de protéger l'espace humanitaire au niveau de la zone. Veiller au respect des politiques, directives et procédures du NRC, et assumer une responsabilité spécifique pour les politiques et procédures HAS. Responsabilités particulières Préparer et animer des séances d'initiation à la HAS pour le nouveau personnel de la zone, ainsi que des séances d'information et des débriefings avec des collègues ou des visiteurs, en partageant les informations pertinentes sur les lieux des activités, en mettant l'accent sur les mesures pratiques de prévention et d'atténuation des risques en matière de sûreté et de sécurité et les mécanismes de signalement. Tenir à jour toutes les informations nécessaires pour les documents HAS, y compris la planification de mission sûre (SMP), les procédures opérationnelles normalisées (SOP), le plan d'hibernation, de relocalisation et d'évacuation (HRE) et le plan d'évacuation médicale (MEDEVAC). Effectuer des évaluations de site pour tous les nouveaux locaux locatifs et fournir toutes les mesures de sûreté et de sécurité à prendre en compte avant utilisation. Assurer le suivi de la mise en œuvre des mesures identifiées pour ces infrastructures. S'assurer que les mouvements des véhicules et du personnel sont surveillés conformément aux procédures et que l'équipement de sûreté et de sécurité nécessaire à l'intérieur de chaque véhicule est disponible et en bon état. Accompagner régulièrement des collègues et/ou des visiteurs sur le terrain pour identifier, planifier et mettre en œuvre des procédures HAS, enrichir les évaluations des risques de sécurité et aider à obtenir et à maintenir un accès humanitaire. Demandez ou générez la création d'utilisateurs pour le nouveau personnel de la zone dans le système de demande d'autorisation de voyage en ligne. Vérifier et approuver les demandes de voyage pour les activités et les visites dans la région. Tenir à jour l'arborescence de communication du personnel de la zone et effectuer des activations de tests. Assurer la formation nécessaire à l'utilisation correcte des dispositifs des systèmes de communication alternatifs, en coordination avec les équipes de support. Après la certification, faciliter la planification et l'exécution de la formation à la sécurité individuelle en environnement hostile (HEIST), des premiers secours sur le terrain et de la formation à la sécurité incendie périodiquement pour le personnel de la zone, en tenant à jour le suivi de la formation correspondante. Promouvoir et faciliter le signalement, la documentation et soutenir la gestion des incidents de HAS dans la région. Faciliter l'hibernation ou la relocalisation du personnel dans les situations d'urgence. Promouvoir les principes et les engagements en matière de sauvegarde au sein de NRC et parmi les bénéficiaires desservis par NRC. Effectuer toute autre tâche liée à HAS et au poste déléguée par le supérieur hiérarchique. Travailler avec la direction pour s'assurer que tout le personnel donne son consentement éclairé sur la base d'un briefing à son arrivée et que des mises à jour sont régulièrement partagées sur le contexte de sécurité. Sous la direction du gestionnaire HAS, contribuer à l'amélioration de l'accès humanitaire pour les opérations du NRC dans la région en aidant les équipes à développer des stratégies d'accès et des plans d'engagement. Collaborer avec les membres du groupe de gestion sectorielle (AMG) et le gestionnaire de la gestion des services de sécurité pour gérer les incidents liés à l'accès, à la sûreté et à la sécurité au niveau de la zone, en veillant à ce qu'ils soient documentés dans NRC Protect. Lorsqu'il est désigné par la direction, diriger et/ou conseiller sur l'engagement avec les parties au conflit, y compris les groupes armés non étatiques et les forces armées étatiques au niveau de la zone. Fournir aux bailleurs de fonds les informations HAS requises pour les propositions de projets, les audits internes ou externes et toute autre demande de la direction de la zone ou de l'ASA. Participer à la gestion du cycle du projet, en fournissant une analyse contextuelle et des conseils techniques sur les modalités opérationnelles et programmatiques. En collaboration avec le responsable de la HAS et les points focaux des partenariats, contribuer aux initiatives de renforcement des capacités et de partage des connaissances avec les partenaires locaux concernant la gestion des risques de sécurité et l'accès humanitaire dans la zone. Représenter NRC dans les forums externes au niveau de la zone, tels que les groupes de coordination de la sécurité, le groupe de travail sur l'accès humanitaire (HAWG) et la coordination CivMalil, ainsi que dans d'autres forums à la demande du responsable de zone et du responsable HAS. Échelle et portée du poste Responsabilité financière : N/A Responsabilité des ressources : NRC Protect et NRC Voyager Interfaces critiques Membres du groupe d'administration de secteur pour la gestion des risques de sécurité, la gestion des incidents, la mise en œuvre des mesures d'atténuation et les priorités interfonctionnelles. Responsable du soutien régional et équipe logistique pour la collaboration sur la conformité en matière de sécurité de tous les bureaux et locaux d'hébergement du NRC, les SOP de sécurité des conducteurs et la formation. Équipe des personnes et de l'organisation de la zone (P&O) pour assurer le devoir de diligence et coordonner le renforcement des capacités du personnel. Équipe des finances de la zone pour les contributions aux budgets liées à la HAS. Compétence clé du personnel pour la sensibilité aux conflits, la criticité des programmes, le principe de « ne pas nuire », l'analyse des besoins humanitaires et les modalités de mise en œuvre. Lorsqu'il est présent, le plomb Protection contre la violence est une interface clé. Points focaux d'accès et de sécurité/sûreté dans les organisations paires pour le partage d'informations, le plaidoyer conjoint, la formation conjointe et les opérations au niveau de la zone. Autorisations d'engagement pour permettre un accès et une exécution du programme sûrs et dans le respect de principes. Qualifications Compétences Les compétences sont importantes pour que l’employé et l’organisation puissent obtenir les résultats souhaités. Compréhension fondamentale des principes humanitaires et de leur application dans les réponses programmatiques et de plaidoyer, la sécurité des ONG et la gestion des risques, et l'accès humanitaire. Expérience antérieure de travail dans des contextes complexes. Maîtrise des applications MS Office, y compris Word et Excel. Maîtrise professionnelle de la langue pertinente (français ), à l'écrit et à l'oral. Contexte/Compétences, connaissances et expérience spécifiques : Expérience de la liaison avec les communautés et les autorités ainsi qu'avec les ONG. La maîtrise de l'anglais et/ou de la conversation et du zarma est une valeur ajoutée Competences comportementales (max 6) Gestion d'un environnement non sécurisé Planification et obtention de résultats Travailler avec les gens Analyse Communiquer avec impact et respect Faire face au changement About Us The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people. At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion. Together, we save lives and rebuild futures. Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to: treat everyone with respect and dignity contribute to building a safe environment for all never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH) always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH About The Team The Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (IDMC) is the world’s authoritative source of data and analysis on internal displacement. Since our establishment in 1998 as part of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC), we offer a rigorous, transparent and independent service to the international community, and inform policy and operational decisions to improve the lives of people living in, or at risk of, internal displacement. With a team of more than 30 people in Geneva and an annual budget of over 5 million USD, we monitor more than 130 countries in the world for which we provide verified, consolidated and multi-sourced estimates of the number of people internally displaced or at risk of becoming displaced by conflict, violence, disasters and development projects. review_candidates.title: Head of Deployments, Africa
review_candidates.description: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About You And The Role Zipline is entering its biggest build period in Africa yet. Over the next two years we will open more than 20 new distribution sites across Nigeria and Côte d’Ivoire, and launch our first Precision Delivery network in Kigali, Rwanda. As Head of Deployments, Africa, you will own every launch from signed contract to a certified, operating site, and make each one faster and more repeatable than the last. Every site should be handed over ready to run, with no open issues left for the operating team. You will lead parallel launch teams across several countries, own the playbook every launch runs on, and build an organisation that scales up for a build wave and back down when it’s done. You will report to the Head of Operations, Africa, and work alongside the Heads of Service Delivery and Logistics as one regional leadership team. What You'll Do Lead parallel launch programmes across Nigeria and Côte d’Ivoire, taking each site from signed contract through land, permits, construction, power, hiring, training and commissioning to handover. Drive the work, not just coordinate it. Set the pace on every launch, hold owners to their dates and the quality bar, and step in early when a launch starts to slip. Run our first Precision Delivery launch in Kigali as a dedicated workstream, with a clear go/no-go gate and dependencies agreed with our platform and engineering teams. Own the deployment playbook and standard bill of materials, and productise them so each launch is faster than the last. Plan each country as a single programme, with one customs plan, one spares plan and one power strategy per country. Hand over every site through a written acceptance gate that the operating team can refuse, and own the cost of any defects in the first 90 days after handover. Build and lead a flexible team: a small permanent core covering programme management, operations readiness, construction, electrical and commercial, plus in-country launch pods and contract build labour. Hire and develop strong leaders, and redeploy talent well as each build wave winds down. Partner closely with Country Directors, governments and regulators, contractors, Supply Chain and Logistics, and Engineering to clear the path for every launch. What Success Looks Like Sites go live certified and on plan, and time to launch falls with every launch. Sites are accepted first time, with few defects in the first 90 days. Every site is delivered on or under budget. The Kigali Precision Delivery launch clears its gates on schedule. Every new launch starts from the playbook. What You'll Bring 12–15+ years delivering multi-site infrastructure or network build programmes, such as telecom tower rollouts, renewable energy, logistics hubs, data centres or fulfilment networks at scale. Hands-on build experience in Africa, covering land, permits, customs, power, contractors and government interfaces. Experience in West Africa is especially valued. A track record of running parallel builds against a contractual deadline. Experience building a repeatable deployment playbook and applying it across many sites. Senior enough to set strategy and lead leaders; hands-on enough to walk a site and see what needs fixing. Comfort leading an organisation that grows and shrinks with the launch pipeline. Strong programme and project management instincts: you drive workstreams end to end across teams you don't directly lead. Excellent stakeholder and negotiation skills, with a track record of aligning senior commercial leaders around a plan and holding a quality bar under delivery pressure. If you believe you have been targeted by a fraudulent party, we ask that you immediately get in touch with us via email at security@flyzipline.com upon receiving a suspicious offer or claim.
